name: Gloaming-Spire
description: Gloaming-Spire is a small, frigid rocky world bristling with tall needle-like rock formations that cast extraordinarily long shadows in the weak light of its distant star. The spires reach heights of several kilometers, their bases buried in frost-shattered boulder fields that crunch underfoot in the thin air.

The light here never rises above a dim gloaming, casting everything in shades of deep blue and grey. The thin atmosphere carries enough dust to scatter the starlight into a faint halo effect around the spires, giving them an ethereal quality that belies their harsh mineral composition.

The spire formations are a geological puzzle, their extreme height-to-width ratios possible only because of the low gravity and absence of significant weathering. Core samples suggest they are remnants of a much thicker crust that has been eroded away over billions of years, leaving only the hardest mineral columns standing.

The planet offers modest mineral resources and serves primarily as a navigation waypoint in a sparsely charted sector. Its stark beauty has made it a minor destination for those willing to travel far for an extraordinary vista.
